name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Tacos
pitch: Roasted sweet potato and spiced black beans make surprisingly hearty tacos — simple but genuinely satisfying.
steps: Peel and dice the sweet potato into small cubes, toss with oil, cumin, and a pinch of chili powder, then roast at 425°F for 20 minutes until caramelized.
While the potato roasts, warm the black beans in a small pan with garlic, a splash of soy sauce, and a pinch of cumin.
Serve everything in warm tortillas — a squeeze of vinegar or hot sauce brightens it right up.
Top with whatever you have: shredded cabbage, sour cream, or just salt and pepper.

name: Black Bean & Sweet Potato Soup
pitch: This is a cozy, warming bowl that practically makes itself — deeply flavorful with just pantry spices doing the heavy lifting.
steps: Dice the sweet potato and sauté in a pot with oil and garlic over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Add the black beans, 3–4 cups of water, a big pinch of cumin, smoked paprika if you have it, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 15–20 minutes until the sweet potato is very tender.
Use a fork or the back of a spoon to mash some of the beans and potato right in the pot — this thickens it beautifully without any extra work.
toolSuggestion: immersion blender (optional, for a smoother texture)

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Rice Bowl
pitch: This is one of those meals that feels like more than the sum of its parts — a warm, filling bowl that comes together fast.
steps: Cook rice according to package directions (about 2 cups water per 1 cup rice, 18 minutes simmered covered).
Meanwhile, cube and pan-fry the sweet potato in butter or oil over medium-high heat, seasoning with garlic, salt, pepper, and a little cumin, until golden and tender — about 12–15 minutes.
Warm the black beans separately with a splash of soy sauce and a pinch of garlic powder.
Assemble: rice on the bottom, sweet potato and beans on top, drizzle with a little vinegar for brightness.
